title: Cyclic root cover, logarithmic eigensheaves and differential blocks
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Y$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme] of pure dimension $n\geq0$. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $m\geq2$, and $0\ne s\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes m})$ whose zero scheme $D=Z(s)$ [def-pc-zero-scheme] is smooth over $F$, allowing $D=\varnothing$. Tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; put $L^{-a}=(L^\vee)^{\otimes a}$, where $L^\vee=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(L,\mathcal O_Y)$. Write $\Omega^1_{Y/F}$ for the sheaf obtained by gluing the modules of Kähler differentials on affine opens [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf].
Form the $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{m-1}L^{-a}$: products with exponent at least $m$ are reduced using contraction with $s:L^{-m}\to\mathcal O_Y$. Let $f:W=\operatorname{Spec}_Y\mathcal A\to Y$, meaning the scheme obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}(A[t]/(t^m-u))$ on affine trivializations $L|_U=\mathcal O_U e$, $s|_U=u e^m$. Then $f$ is finite locally free of rank $m$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] (in particular inverse images of affine opens are affine), and $W$ is smooth projective over $F$, of pure dimension $n$; connectedness of $W$ is not asserted.
Define $\Omega^1_{Y/F}(\log D)$ as the subsheaf of rational one-forms locally generated by regular one-forms and $du/u$ for a local equation $u$ of $D$. For $D=\varnothing$ this is $\Omega^1_{Y/F}$. There is an $\mathcal O_Y$-linear map $\operatorname{res}_D:\Omega^1_{Y/F}(\log D)\to\mathcal O_D$, where $\mathcal O_D$ is regarded as a sheaf on $Y$, characterized locally by $\operatorname{res}_D(\alpha+b\,du/u)=b\bmod u$ for regular $\alpha$.
There are canonical decompositions of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules
$$f_*\mathcal O_W=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{m-1}L^{-a},\qquad f_*\Omega^1_{W/F}=\Omega^1_{Y/F}\oplus\bigoplus_{a=1}^{m-1}\bigl(\Omega^1_{Y/F}(\log D)\otimes L^{-a}\bigr).$$
The summands indexed by $a$ have character $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^a$ for the action $t\mapsto\zeta t$ of the $m$th roots of unity. For $1\leq a<m$, the $F$-linear universal derivation $d:\mathcal O_W\to\Omega^1_{W/F}$ has block $\nabla_a:L^{-a}\to\Omega^1_{Y/F}(\log D)\otimes L^{-a}$ given on the above trivialization by
$$\nabla_a(b e^{-a})=\left(db+\frac{a}{m}b\,\frac{du}{u}\right)\otimes e^{-a}.$$
For every $q\geq0$ the canonical cohomology comparisons for this finite morphism give
$$H^q(W,\mathcal O_W)\cong\bigoplus_{a=0}^{m-1}H^q(Y,L^{-a}),$$
$$H^q(W,\Omega^1_{W/F})\cong H^q(Y,\Omega^1_{Y/F})\oplus\bigoplus_{a=1}^{m-1}H^q(Y,\Omega^1_{Y/F}(\log D)\otimes L^{-a}).$$
Under these comparisons $H^q(W,d)$ respects characters and its $a$th block is $H^q(Y,\nabla_a)$. Here ordinary module sheaf cohomology is [pqf-def-cohomology]; cohomology maps for $F$-linear sheaf maps such as $d$ and $\nabla_a$ are computed after restricting to sheaves of $F$-vector spaces on the Zariski topology, using their canonical agreement with module cohomology on these objects. No assertion that $d$ or $\nabla_a$ is $\mathcal O$-linear is made.

source.place: WANTED locally: Popa, Kodaira dimension of algebraic varieties, Proposition 1.6.5 and its proof, printed pp.24--26; first two cohomology displays and character compatibility in proof of Theorem 1.6.6, pp.26--27; local differential formula in Lemma 1.6.7, p.27. Read online at https://people.math.harvard.edu/~mpopa/271/Kodaira-posted.pdf. Logarithmic residue also checked in literature/stacks-project/derham.tex, Tag 0FMW (lemma-log-complex), degree one.

proof.text: On a nonempty affine trivialization, $s=u e^m$ with $u\ne0$. Indeed a section of a line bundle on an integral scheme which vanishes on a nonempty open vanishes everywhere: on any intersecting trivialization its coefficient vanishes in a localization of a domain and hence is zero; irreducibility makes those intersections nonempty. Thus $u$ is a nonzerodivisor. The local zero scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/(u))$, so $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor, possibly empty. Choose frames with $e_j=g e_i$ on an overlap. Then $u_j=g^{-m}u_i$, and $t_j=g^{-1}t_i$ identifies the two root algebras. Associativity of the displayed multiplication is checked by reducing a monomial of total exponent $r$ to $u^{\lfloor r/m\rfloor}t^{r\bmod m}$; the result is independent of parentheses. The frame changes preserve this multiplication and satisfy the cocycle equation.

source.place: Effective Cartier divisors: local nonzerodivisor definition; elementary construction from the specified section

proof.text: Each $L^{-a}$ is locally a free rank-one module, so their finite direct sum with the multiplication of step 1 is a quasi-coherent algebra. The relative-spectrum theorem constructs $f$ and identifies $f_*\mathcal O_W$ with this algebra, including the affine inverse-image assertion. On a frame chart its algebra is $B=A[t]/(t^m-u)$ and the monic-quotient power basis is $1,t,\ldots,t^{m-1}$. Hence it is finite free of rank $m$ over $A$. In particular it is flat, since tensoring with $A^m$ is the finite direct sum of the identity functor; its algebra presentation has one generator and one relation. Thus $f$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, and every fibre algebra has dimension $m$. This is finite locally free of rank $m$ in the cited convention.

source.place: Tags 01SA (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras), 01WH (definition-integral); monic division and the local definition of finite locally free

proof.text:
We shall use the following explicit differential calculation on each root chart. The universal property identifies
$$\Omega_{B/F}=\bigl((B\otimes_A\Omega_{A/F})\oplus B\,dt\bigr)/(du-mt^{m-1}dt).$$
To check the identification, a derivation to any $B$-module $N$ is specified by its restriction $\delta:A\to N$ and $v=\delta(t)$; it descends from $A[t]$ to $B$ exactly when $\delta(u)=mt^{m-1}v$. Conversely the formula $\delta(\sum b_i t^i)=\sum t^i\delta(b_i)+\sum i b_i t^{i-1}v$ supplies it. This proves the presentation by the universal property, and the construction commutes with restrictions because it sends each $db$ to the same universal differential. No left exactness of a general conormal sequence is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega); elementary verification of the differential presentation

proof.text:
At $y\in D$, put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $I=(u)$. Since $u$ is a nonzerodivisor, $R/(u)\to I/I^2$, $b\mapsto bu$, is an isomorphism: $bu\in(u^2)$ implies $b\in(u)$. The conormal-fibre injection for the smooth source $D$ therefore says $du\ne0$ in $\Omega_{Y/F}\otimes\kappa(y)$. Since $Y$ is smooth of pure dimension $n$, its differential sheaf is locally free of rank $n$. After choosing a basis, some coefficient of $du$ is a unit near $y$. Replace that basis vector by $du$ and shrink to obtain
$$\Omega_{A/F}=A\,du\oplus M,\qquad M\cong A^{n-1}.$$
This argument concerns a point of $D$, so $n\ge1$ there. It does not assume that an arbitrary defining equation already belongs to an etale coordinate system. Away from $D$, only the ordinary local freeness of $\Omega_{Y/F}$ will be used.

The ambient $Y\times_F\mathbf A^1_F$ is smooth: its projection to $Y$ is an affine-space projection and composition preserves smoothness. The root chart is the zero scheme of the section $t^m-u$ of the trivial line bundle on $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$, by the affine-local form of zero schemes. At a point above $D$, $t=0$ in the residue field and $d(t^m-u)=-du\ne0$ by step 4. At a point outside $D$, $t$ is a unit and the coefficient $mt^{m-1}$ of $dt$ is a unit, since $\operatorname{char}F=0$. The smooth-hypersurface criterion applies at every point, proving that $W$ is smooth over $F$.
In the first case the presentation of step 3 eliminates $du$, giving $\Omega_{B/F}=B\,dt\oplus(B\otimes_A M)$ of rank $n$. In the second it eliminates $dt$, giving $\Omega_{B/F}=B\otimes_A\Omega_{A/F}$ of rank $n$. The smooth dimension/differential-rank theorem gives local topological dimension $n$ everywhere on $W$.

Apply the finite-over-projective theorem with $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$, $T=Y$ and $h=f$. Its Noetherian-base hypothesis holds because a field has only the ideals $0$ and $F$, and $S$ is affine. The theorem gives a global projective-space embedding of $W$ over $F$, not merely projectivity in the projective-bundle convention. In particular $W$ is of finite type over $F$ and is Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian theorem. Applying the constant-local-dimension component theorem with the open equal to all of $W$ and step 5 shows that every irreducible component has dimension $n$. This proves the stated pure dimension. No connectedness is used or deduced.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); finite-over-projective input is also in the latest blueprint lem-fin-finite-over-projective.proof.md

proof.text:
The splitting of step 4 also proves the residue assertion directly. Locally near $D$, logarithmic forms are
$$A\,(du/u)\oplus M\ \subset\ (\Omega_{A/F})[1/u].$$
Here $u$ is a nonzerodivisor on the free differential module. Send $c\,du/u+\eta$ to $c\bmod u$. A regular form has coefficient divisible by $u$ in the first summand, so this gives exactly $\alpha+b\,du/u\mapsto b\bmod u$, independently of its expression. Replacing $u$ by $h u$ for a unit $h$ changes $du/u$ by the regular form $dh/h$ and leaves the residue unchanged. Consequently the local maps agree on overlaps. Off $D$ the logarithmic module is the ordinary differential module and the target is zero. Thus they glue to the claimed $\mathcal O_Y$-linear map; if $D$ is empty it is the zero map to the zero sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0FMW (lemma-log-complex), degree-one local residue calculation; written out using step 4

proof.text: The automorphism $t\mapsto\zeta t$ is compatible with $t^m=u$ and with all frame changes, so defines the specified action. On the power basis of step 2 its weight-$a$ submodule is $At^a$, with transition $t_j^a=g^{-a}t_i^a$; these are precisely the transitions of $L^{-a}$. Since $F$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, it has $m$ distinct $m$th roots of unity and a primitive one: for the latter elementary field-theory input use the primitive-root theorem cited below. Distinct powers of a primitive root are distinct scalars, so the diagonal action on this basis has exactly these eigenspaces. This establishes the structure-sheaf character decomposition, including the invariant summand $a=0$.

source.place: Power-basis calculation; roots-of-unity input as cited

proof.text: Define the differential-summand map for $a>0$ by $(\alpha\otimes e^{-a})\mapsto t^a f^*\alpha$ as a rational differential expression. It is regular: near $D$, $t^a du/u=m t^{a-1}dt$, and $t^a\eta$ is regular for $\eta\in M$; off $D$, $u,t$ are units. At a branch chart, step 3 gives the free $A$-basis consisting of $t^jdt$ and $t^j\eta_i$ ($0\le j<m$). Their weights are respectively $j+1$ and $j$ modulo $m$. Thus the invariant module is generated by $t^{m-1}dt=du/m$ and the $\eta_i$, namely $\Omega_{A/F}$; for $1\le a<m$ the weight-$a$ basis is $t^{a-1}dt,t^a\eta_i$. The proposed map carries the logarithmic basis $du/u,\eta_i$ to $m t^{a-1}dt,t^a\eta_i$, an invertible diagonal change of basis. Off $D$, step 3 gives $\Omega_{B/F}=B\otimes_A\Omega_{A/F}$ and the same conclusion follows from the power basis. Finally $e_j=g e_i$, $t_j=g^{-1}t_i$ gives $t_j^a\alpha_j=t_i^a g^{-a}\alpha_j$, exactly the tensor transition. These maps glue to the asserted canonical character decomposition of $f_*\Omega^1_{W/F}$.

source.place: Universal derivation and explicit bases of steps 2--4; Popa Proposition 1.6.5 local computation adapted algebraically

proof.text:
Apply the derivation rule to a function in the weight-$a$ summand:
$$d(bt^a)=t^a\,db+a b t^{a-1}dt=t^a\bigl(db+(a/m)b\,du/u\bigr).$$
The first equality holds in $\Omega_{B/F}$; the second uses the regular interpretation of the logarithmic expression in step 9. This is exactly the displayed formula for $\nabla_a$. On an overlap $e_j=g e_i$, the same section has coefficients $b_j=g^a b_i$ and $u_j=g^{-m}u_i$; hence
$$db_j+(a/m)b_j\,du_j/u_j=g^a\bigl(db_i+(a/m)b_i\,du_i/u_i\bigr),$$
as the two terms involving $dg$ cancel. Thus the block formula really glues. The invariant block is the ordinary $d$ on $Y$. Applying an automorphism to $dc$ gives $d$ of the transformed $c$, so $d$ respects the character action. All these maps are $F$-linear; the displayed $db$ term explains why they need not be $\mathcal O_Y$-linear.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), Leibniz rule; Popa Lemma 1.6.7 local formula, with general exponent a

proof.text: Use projectivity of $Y$ (hence properness and separatedness) and its finite-type Noetherian property to choose a finite affine open cover $\mathcal U$. Its tuple intersections are affine by the separated affine-intersection theorem. Their inverse images under $f$ are affine by step 2, giving a finite affine-intersection cover $f^{-1}\mathcal U$ of $W$. All sheaves occurring in the two decompositions are quasi-coherent: on the charts above the logarithmic and ordinary differential sheaves and the line powers are finite free, and affine pushforward preserves quasi-coherence. Affine quasi-coherent cohomology vanishes in positive degrees on each affine open subscheme, and the open-restriction comparison identifies this cohomology of the open subscheme with the right derived functors of sections over that open computed in modules on the whole scheme. The general ringed-site module/abelian comparison transfers this acyclicity to underlying abelian sheaves, and also identifies cohomology computed in sheaves of $F$-vector spaces (apply it to the constant ring sheaf $F$); the enough-injectives condition is provided by the ringed-space theorem for both ring sheaves. Thus the acyclic Cech-edge theorem applies to all these sheaves and to arbitrary additive maps between them, including $d$ and $\nabla_a$.

For $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_W$ or $\Omega^1_{W/F}$ the section complexes satisfy the literal equality
$$\check C(\mathcal U,f_*\mathcal G)=\check C(f^{-1}\mathcal U,\mathcal G):$$
both have the same sections on every tuple intersection, and the same alternating restriction differentials. The site-change square in the acyclic Cech-edge theorem identifies this equality with the canonical cohomology comparison for $f$. At the complex level a finite direct sum of sheaves gives the finite direct sum of these section complexes; kernels and images are componentwise, so taking $H^q$ gives the two displayed cohomology decompositions. Apply the same theorem's coefficient-naturality square to $f_*d$ and to every character inclusion and projection. By step 10 their section maps are block diagonal, with blocks $\nabla_a$, so their cohomology maps have blocks $H^q(Y,\nabla_a)$. The theorem's forgetting square identifies these with the specified module-cohomology comparisons, while its additive naturality gives the maps for $F$-linear sheaf morphisms. This proves the last assertion for every $q\ge0$, including degree zero.
